name: Platonism
summary: Platonism holds that reality's true objects are unchanging Forms, crowned by the Form of the Good, knowable by reason rather than the senses. Its political implications, as scholars draw them from the Republic and Laws, are that justice means each part of the city and soul doing its proper task, that those who know the good should rule, and that education and law should aim at the virtue of citizens. It is hostile to democracy as rule by the unlearned and favours regulation of wealth and culture.
scope: Platonism as a political philosophy, drawn from Plato's Republic and Laws and the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy's accounts of them. Neoplatonism, modern Platonism about abstract objects and Plato's other dialogues are not the basis. The Republic and Laws differ (the Laws drops guardian communism and philosopher rule for law and a mixed constitution); where they differ on a statement the answer is a split.

sources.title: Plato's Ethics and Politics in The Republic
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Philosopher rulers, classes, guardians' property and family, women guardians, education, censorship, noble lie, rule of law.

sources.title: The Republic
sources.author: Plato (tr. Benjamin Jowett)
sources.usedFor: Philosophers as kings (Book V), censorship of poets and tales (Books II-III), the origin of war from luxury (Book II), state use of falsehood.

sources.title: Plato's Laws
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Mixed constitution, land allotments and wealth limits, penalties aimed at reform, impiety laws, persuasive preludes, exclusion of crafts.

sources.title: The Laws (Project Gutenberg, tr. Benjamin Jowett)
sources.author: Plato
sources.usedFor: Land allotments, wealth classes, office, education, religion, penalties, trade and foreigners in the second-best city.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Republic's guardians are a trained warrior class and the Laws trains all citizens for war.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The principle of specialization, each doing the one task they are best suited for, underlies justice in the city.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Republic selects guardians by nature, not birth, and allows children to move between classes.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic replaces guardian families with state-arranged unions, which is not abolition of legal recognition of marriage.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about prisons or punishment, and the statement now asks only whether the police should be abolished.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic limits medical care for the chronically ill, which does not settle funding research on slowing ageing.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Laws V makes the 5040 citizens owners of the land and protectors of their lots, and says tilling land in common goes beyond what its citizens can bear, though the lots are inalienable and the earth sacred to the gods.

allow-dual-citizenship.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Laws bars private holdings of gold and silver, but it states nothing on payments untraceable to the government.

apologise-for-past-wrongs.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

automation-leaves-most-without-work.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

ban-interest.rationale: Laws V says no one shall lend money upon interest and the borrower owes neither capital nor interest, and that gold, silver and moneylending have no place in the city.

ban-patents-on-life.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

ban-spanking.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

build-apartments-freely.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

capital-controls.rationale: The Laws bars citizens from owning gold or silver and restricts foreign travel and trade, so the state controls money crossing the border.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Republic subjects poets and nursery tales to state censorship so that guardians grow up virtuous.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Laws VI mixes election and lot for the council, but neither work proposes lot-chosen assemblies deliberating on public questions.

civil-disobedience-accept-penalty.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

civil-marriage.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic concerns rule inside a city, not rule of one society over another.

class-collaboration.rationale: Justice in the city is each class doing its own work in harmony, with no struggle between classes.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Republic VIII-IX derives regimes from the characters of men and the decline of the ruling class, and nowhere states class conflict as the main driver of history.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule belongs to philosophers, not priests, though religion is supported by law.

collective-farming.rationale: The Laws divides land into household allotments and rejects farming in common.

colonial-socialism-democratic-stage.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Republic makes the unity of the city the highest political good and has those who know the good rule for all, which leaves no place for separate community electorates.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Honour- and gain-seeking are marks of defective regimes, not engines of progress.

conscription.rationale: Defense is a duty of the guardians, and the Laws expects citizens to take part in defense.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Laws III calls the rule of the wise a rule of law over willing subjects, not compulsion, but the Republic has rulers govern the many by their own knowledge and by a founding falsehood; its words point both ways.

constitution-recognises-indigenous-natio.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

constitutional-jury-trial.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Republic holds that luxury and the pursuit of unlimited wealth corrupt the city and cause war, and the Laws limit wealth to keep citizens virtuous.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic gives power to philosopher-rulers and states nothing on small self-governing cooperative communities.

country-wealth-only-from-land.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Laws make law, not the will of the many, supreme and Plato is hostile to rule by majority.

criminalize-genocide-denial.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

democracy-becomes-oligarchy.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

democracy-best.rationale: The Republic presents democracy as a degenerate regime on the road to tyranny, and the Laws prefers a mixture of monarchy and democracy.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic criticises democracy as a regime but does not address whether fair elections alone make a government democratic.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

democratic-peace.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic judges democracy a defective regime but never discusses spreading it or its effect on peace.

destroy-worshipped-objects.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule by the producing class over others contradicts rule by the wise.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Neither the Republic nor the Laws has an elected head of state.

direct-votes.rationale: Rule by the unlearned many is the defect of democracy; decisions belong to those with knowledge.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Republic argues that women can be educated and rule as guardians, so law should not fix separate public roles.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Laws V judges wealth by proportion to worth and by the city's unity, which is neither a process test nor an equality test.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Nulled (later pass): A modern claim the Republic and Laws do not address.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Justice means each part performing its function for the whole, and the city's unity outranks individual claims.

dynastic-succession.rationale: In the Republic rulers are chosen by nature and education, and guardians' children who lack the right nature are demoted, so inheritance of office is rejected.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Laws seeks a self-sufficient city but says nothing on a colonial empire.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic reports the popular charge that philosophers are useless, but only to answer it; it states no view on the educated in general.

elective-rulers.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Neither the Republic nor the Laws has a single elected head of state.

elite-replacement.rationale: Nulled (later pass): A modern conspiracy claim on which the Republic and Laws state nothing.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The ideal city controls education, stories and art to produce unity and virtue, so social pressure to conform is endorsed rather than resisted.

equal-conscription.rationale: Republic V has women guardians train and fight alongside men, so any duty to defend the city falls on both sexes.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Laws V sets honours by proportion to worth rather than equally, but the work states nothing on equal legal rights as such.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Justice is each doing the task suited to them, with unequal roles; guardians are communal but the classes differ.

ethnicity-statistics.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

evolved-behavioural-sex-differences.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

exclude-trans-women-women-only-spaces.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Neither work states a view on whether leaving a country is a check on government.

experts-over-public.rationale: Central: cities will not be free of evils until philosophers rule, since only those who know the good should govern.

femininity-compatible-with-feminism.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Laws VIII lets resident foreigners register property for up to twenty years but does not say whether they may own land.

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

four-day-week.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The Republic and Laws prescribe a fixed blueprint for the city's economy and property, and reject letting people choose their own arrangements.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

freedom-is-self-government-of-desire.rationale: Republic IV calls a man master of himself when reason rules his lower desires, slave of himself when badly educated, and Republic IX calls the soul ruled by desire enslaved.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Republic V argues the natures of men and women differ only in degree for the purpose of ruling; it never says gender is a social construct.

generational-constitutional-review.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

government-nudges.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

gradual-change.rationale: Laws VII warns that changing even children's games breeds a taste for new institutions and calls for permanence, while the Republic (Book V) holds that cities have no rest from evil until philosophers rule, a thorough remaking.

harm-principle.rationale: The city is to make citizens virtuous, using censorship and laws against impiety, not merely to prevent harm.

head-of-state-dissolves-parliament.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Regulation of guardian reproduction by the city is part of the Republic; this audit did not read the specific passage.

homestead-ownership.rationale: In the Republic the guardians hold no private property and in the Laws land allotments are fixed and inalienable, so ownership is set by the community, not by first claim.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: Laws IV reports as a true tradition a blessed age under Cronos, ruled by demigods, and says present cities must imitate it as far as they can.

humans-entitled-to-use-animals.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

immigration-favours-shared-culture.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

independent-unions.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Neither work has trade unions.

indigenous-internal-justice.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Laws regulates marriage and state religion but never mentions marriage between members of different religions.

keep-public-institutions-small.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

land-redistribution.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Laws allots equal lots in a new foundation; it does not call for taking existing estates from owners.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about community or state ownership of land, and the statement now asks only whether a right to hold land should end when the holder stops using it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Plato has no scripture; the Laws traces its code to reason and to oracles such as Delphi, so the statement about scripture is not one he answers.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic and Laws do not address public ownership of local services.

local-veto-new-housing.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

mandatory-environmental-reporting.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Laws fixes penalties in its code for some offences and lets judges assess others, so it does not settle mandatory minimums for repeat offenders.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Republic says brave guardians who fall in war are honoured as a golden race and as divine spirits.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic and Laws regulate culture to shape character but do not state that mass entertainment pacifies people.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Republic VIII ties regimes partly to wealth and partly to the characters of men and breeding, so it does not settle economic structure as the main cause of change.

maximum-personal-income.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic parallels justice in city and soul but never states that the means of reform must mirror the goal.

media-academia-power.rationale: Nulled (later pass): A factual claim about modern institutions that the Republic and Laws do not address.

member-state-blocks-federal-overreach.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The guardian class of auxiliaries defends and keeps order in the Republic, but under the rule of philosophers.

military-organisation-revolutionary-part.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

minority-veto.rationale: Wise rule binds all citizens, and the Republic gives no consent-based veto to those who disagree.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The Laws recommends a constitution that blends monarchic and democratic elements, as the SEP describes.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Mixed: the Laws treats monarchy as one good element of a constitution, but the Republic's rulers are chosen by nature and education, and children are reassigned by merit, against hereditary rule.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

moral-incentives.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic motivates guardians by honour, but producers work for their own gain; it does not make duty the main motive for work generally.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Laws requires belief in gods who care for humans and punishes impiety, and the Republic makes piety part of justice.

municipal-businesses-mixed-economy.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

municipal-property.rationale: In the Republic the guardians hold property in common and the producers keep private property, so neither local community ownership nor markets are the model.

national-church-status.rationale: The Laws sets a state religion, controls cult and punishes impiety, giving official worship a protected legal status.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic and Laws say nothing about national minorities.

natural-rulers.rationale: Central: rulers are chosen for the philosophical nature suited to knowing the good, as against the many.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Laws IX declares a person who kills in self-defence free from guilt, as with killing an enemy, so killing in self-defence is not wrong.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state must foster virtue through education and law, not just protect property and justice.

no-central-bank.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Laws demands obedience to law but also says some constitutions are not true ones; it does not state whether legal status alone binds.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Education in piety and about the gods is part of the city's teaching.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Republic gives rule to guardians selected by long education and repeated testing, not by election, wealth or birth; competitive examination as such is a later institution.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Laws VI fills offices by election with scrutiny and uses the lot only inside that process, so lotteries do not replace elections.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

parents-choose-intersex-surgery.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Neither work has a parliament with supreme lawmaking power, and the Laws makes law, not an assembly, supreme.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Republic treats rule as a craft for trained philosophers and criticises democracy, so ordinary people deciding directly is rejected.

party-own-road.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Communist party strategy lies outside the Republic and Laws.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Republic's education and the noble lie train guardians to love and defend the city, so teaching civic loyalty is stated as a goal; flag and anthem are not named.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic ranks producers lowest and says nothing on joining patriotism to workers' interests.

pay-for-effort.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

pay-off-national-debt.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

person-over-state.rationale: The Republic aims at the happiness of the whole city and not any one class, and subordinates individuals to the city's proper order.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on knowledge and law, not personal oaths.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Plato's guardians hold even homes and goods in common, so private personal possessions are not the rule for the ruling class.

physical-labour-duty.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

political-borders-follow-ecosystems.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about one government, party or regime, or about fighting corruption, not a general claim that most politicians put their own interests first, which this statement now asks.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic and Laws have no press, so they state nothing on press ownership.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

price-stability-first.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defense is the duty of the guardian class and justice is a public function of the city.

production-for-use.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic derives the city from needs yet leaves producers their private earnings; it does not state that need should replace profit as the purpose of production.

prohibit-child-medical-transition.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

promote-ethnic-return-migration.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Laws, the practical Platonic constitution, make law the master of rulers and give each code a persuasive preamble, though the Republic's philosopher-kings are above fixed law.

property-franchise.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Laws VI gives every citizen a lot, so it does not reserve the vote for owners as a principle; the Republic does not address a property franchise.

property-fundamental.rationale: Laws XI says the legislator regards citizens and their possessions as belonging to the family and, still more, to the state, and Republic III-IV has guardians own no property.

property-sabotage-justified.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: In the Republic the guardians hold no property and the Laws treat allotments as the city's, so property is subordinate to the common good.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic has rulers use a founding falsehood but states nothing on a right of access to government information.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Laws, Book X, sets penalties for impiety and for private shrines and false religion, backed by the state.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

racial-community-economic-control.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

racial-oppression-before-sexism.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Neither the Republic nor the Laws classifies people by race, so they state nothing on segregation law.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Knowledge comes through reason and dialectic, though the philosophy also holds a place for myth and piety.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Neither work has elected delegates or a recall; officials answer to scrutineers, not voters.

refuse-to-join-illegitimate-government.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Laws has one city under one lawgiver, with no regions holding delegated powers.

regional-resource-ownership.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

rehabilitation.rationale: The Laws says penalties aim to make offenders more virtuous or less vicious, with deterrence as a further aim.

religion-from-peoples-character.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Laws punish impiety and treat civic religion as necessary for virtue, so religion is not an illusion to fade.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Laws enforces state religion through impiety laws, so adherents would not exempt groups from general law.

religious-nation.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Laws sets a state cult but does not define the national community by shared religion.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

replace-appointed-officials.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic has guardians own nothing, but it concerns appointed guardians, not paid elected representatives.

reserved-seats-excluded-groups.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

restore-past-order.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic and Laws recount a decline from an ideal but neither puts restoration of a lost order above progress.

restrict-private-adult-pornography-acces.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic censors poetry and tales; neither it nor the Laws names pornography.

restrict-technology-exports-to-rivals.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic describes an agricultural simple city, not foraging, and never discusses a return to hunting and gathering.

return-to-pre-conversion-religion.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

rich-first.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Neither work addresses regional development policy.

rule-by-example.rationale: Split: rulers' virtue matters, but the Laws is a full law code with preludes plus penalties.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic censors the poets but never calls for destroying inherited culture.

say-in-proportion-to-effect.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

school-vouchers.rationale: Laws VII makes education compulsory whether parents please or not and says pupils belong to the state rather than their parents, so parents choosing among schools is rejected.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Republic criticises literal stories of gods in the poets and puts religious tales under philosophical censorship, so scripture would not be taken as inerrant and literal.

second-chamber.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Laws has a council and a Nocturnal Council, but neither is described as a second chamber beside a directly elected parliament.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Republic I-IV argues that justice benefits its holder, which does not settle whether pursuing self-interest is morally good.

separate-church-state.rationale: Laws X and XII put impiety under the city's law and place cult, shrines and priests under state officers, so the state is not separate from religion.

separated-powers.rationale: The Laws' mixed constitution divides offices between elective and lot-based elements.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Republic V treats the difference between the sexes as irrelevant to ruling but never states that sex is socially constructed.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The tripartite soul is shared, but neither work grounds human rights in it.

shut-down-tax-havens.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

simple-living.rationale: The Republic's guardians live austerely with limited needs and common meals, and the Laws warns against luxury and excess wealth.

single-common-good.rationale: The city aims at one good, justice, determined by those who know it, and not at balancing interests.

slavery-reparations.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Laws VII calls for permanence and warns against innovation even in children's games, while Republic V says cities will not rest from evils until philosophers rule, a thorough remaking.

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Republic gives rule to philosopher guardians and keeps the producing class from ruling, so workers' political power is not required.

socialized-care.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic has the state rear guardians' children, which covers only part of domestic work.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Laws IV calls rulers servants of the law, but the Republic leaves philosopher-rulers free to act on knowledge and says good rulers will find the laws themselves; its words point both ways.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Justice for the soul and the city is about the Form of the Good, so politics serves the soul as well as material needs.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Republic refutes the claim that rule serves the stronger; true rulers aim at the good of the ruled.

state-finances-worker-businesses.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

state-harmful.rationale: The city is where justice is achieved and the Republic's whole project is to design the best state, so a stateless life is rejected.

state-laws-apply-online.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Laws (Book X) makes denial of the gods a punishable offence and has the state teach piety.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: Laws IV says the legislator aims to persuade citizens to virtue as readily as possible, and Republic II-III has the city's education and censorship build the way of life it judges good.

students-direct-own-learning.rationale: Laws VII makes the curriculum and attendance compulsory, set by law, and the Republic prescribes the education of the guardians, so students do not decide what they learn.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Laws puts religion under the city's law, with state officials supervising shrines and forbidding private cults, so religious bodies serve the polis.

tax-holding-cash.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Republic traces war to expanding beyond needs through luxury.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

total-state.rationale: The ideal city directs education, culture, and economic roles under the rulers, though not as a modern total state.

traditional-family.rationale: The Republic (Book V) abolishes private families among the guardians, while the Laws (Books V and VI) keep households as the unit of the 5040 lots and regulate marriage; its words point both ways.

troops-home-from-abroad.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

turn-back-illegal-migrants.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

unions-run-economy.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

universal-morality.rationale: Republic VI-VII makes the Form of the Good the standard for all virtue, known by reason and the same everywhere.

unpaid-domestic-work-exploitation.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

wages-fall-to-bare-minimum.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

war-builds-character.rationale: Adherents are split: the Republic trains martial guardians, while the Laws criticizes organizing the city around war.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Republic says both wealth and poverty corrupt the city, and the Laws caps property and bars great fortunes so that wealth cannot rule.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Republic VII holds the philosopher's contemplative life is best yet obliges him to return and rule in the ideal city, and VI has him stand aside in corrupt ones; its words point both ways.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Nulled (later pass): Republic V ties women guardians to communal living, but it does not say women's equality requires a changed economic system.

women-organise-apart-from-men.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

workers-own-party.rationale: Nulled (later pass): The Republic has no political parties, so it states nothing on a workers' party.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

youth-equal-civil-rights.rationale: The Republic and Laws record no position on this statement.

missingStatements.text: Art, poetry and stories should be censored if they harm citizens' moral character.
missingStatements.rationale: The Republic puts poetry and tales under state censorship and the Laws also regulates what citizens are taught, so that education serves virtue.

notes: Later pass (2026-11-18) under rules 7: read the Republic and Laws in full text (Project Gutenberg, Jowett) and cited them by book, bringing every answer to what they state; about 58 older answers resting on general inference or on a source not opened were nulled with their history kept, and new statements were answered where the texts speak. Themes searched in the full texts: property and wealth, education, religion and impiety, offices and election, law and punishment, war, women, trade and foreigners, family and marriage, class. The Republic and Laws record nothing on most modern statements (money, migration, technology, parties, sex and gender policy), which stay null.

keyFigures.role: Founder of the Academy and author of the Republic and Laws
